title: Pack a window's low corner level: lift it with an air wedge, slide a packer under, let it down and take the wedge out
instruction: The window's left corner is sitting low on the sill. Get it level on the loose packer, using the air wedge to lift it, and leave nothing but the packers under the window.
context: Every window is set level on plastic packers before it is fixed, and one corner nearly always sits low. The frame is too heavy and too smooth to hold up with one hand while the other packs it, so fitters use an air wedge: a flat bag slid into the gap under the frame and pumped up with a squeeze bulb. It lifts a millimetre or two per squeeze and holds, leaving the hands free to slide the packer in; a button lets the frame back down. The robot has to work a lifting tool, not lift: get a 2 mm bag into a gap of a few millimetres, pump until the corner clears the packer's thickness, place the packer under the corner, lower the frame onto it and get the tool back out. Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031; about 959,000 US jobs in 2024, BLS: "Install structures or fixtures, such as windows, frames, floorings, trim, or hardware") and glaziers (47-2121) do this on every window; kitchen and appliance fitters level cabinets and machines the same way.
setup: Station table (a wooden bench, 75 cm high) with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y toward the left arm; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the bench top. The bench top is the window opening's sill. Opening: two planed pine 2x4 posts (38 x 89 mm, 61.6 cm tall, the 89 mm side along x) screwed upright to the bench, centred at x 43.5, y 48.65 and y -48.65, and a 2x4 head (38 mm thick, 89 mm deep, 101.1 cm long) across their tops, its underside 61.6 cm up: an opening 93.5 cm wide and 61.6 cm high. Four steel mending plates (30 x 70 x 3 mm) are screwed to the head, two on its front face and two on its back, at y 25 and y -25, each hanging 4 cm below it: they stand 9.5 mm clear of the window and keep it from tipping out of the opening. Window: a white uPVC fixed-light (non-opening) window, 91.5 cm wide and 60 cm high, 14 kg: frame profile 7 cm deep with a 6 cm face, glazed with a 24 mm sealed double-glazed unit. It stands in the opening with its room-side face at x 40 (the frame runs from x 40 to x 47), centred on y 0, 1 cm clear of each post. Its right bottom corner rests on a blue plastic flat packer (100 x 28 x 6 mm) lying across the sill under the right jamb, centred at y -42.75, from x 35.5 to x 45.5 (4.5 cm of it showing in front of the frame). Its left bottom corner rests on the sill itself, so the window slopes down to the left: the left corner is 6 mm lower than the right, the gap under the bottom rail tapers from 6 mm at the right to nothing at the left, and the frame's top is 1 cm below the head at the right. Loose packer: an identical blue packer, lying flat on the sill in front of the low corner, long side pointing at the window, centred at x 31, y 42 (its far end 4 cm from the frame). Air wedge (an inflatable lifting bag of the 160 mm class: rated 135 kg, 2 mm thick empty, inflating to 50 mm): a dark grey bag 16 cm (x) by 15 cm (y), 2 mm thick, lying flat on the sill with its centre at x 30.5, y -8 (its far edge 1.5 cm from the frame). At the middle of its near edge, an orange grip block 25 mm long (x), 20 mm wide, 22 mm tall is clamped round the hose where it enters the bag (wood or printed plastic, added so that a parallel gripper can hold the wedge). From the block a black rubber hose, 8 mm across and 75 mm long, runs straight back toward the arms to a black rubber squeeze bulb, 80 mm long and 45 mm across, lying on the sill and centred at x 7.5, y -8. On top of the bulb, 2 cm from its hose end (x 9.5), is the red release button, 14 mm across, standing 4 mm proud. Nothing else is on the bench.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial with a steel rule and the video. Corner height: the gap between the sill and the underside of the frame at its left end (0 at the start; 6 mm when it rests on a packer and the window is level). The packer is in place when the loose packer lies flat on the sill under the frame's left jamb: at least 4 cm of its length under the frame, its centre line 1.4 to 6 cm in from the frame's left end, pointing across the frame (within 20 degrees). 1.0: the corner rests on the packer (packer in place, corner height 4.5 to 7.5 mm), the whole bag is out from under the frame, on the room side of its face, and both grippers are 5 cm or more from the frame, the packer, the bag and its block, the hose and the bulb. 0.75: the corner rests on the packer as above, but part of the bag is still under the frame or a gripper is within 5 cm of any of those. 0.5: the packer is in place but the corner is more than 7.5 mm up (still held up by the wedge). 0.25: the corner is 3 mm or more above the sill and none of the above applies (lifted, but not packed). 0: anything else, including a trial where nothing moves, a corner let back down on the sill, and a packer pushed against or beside the frame without the corner coming up. 0 if the window is pushed off its right packer or out of the opening. How it is done is free: which arm does what, how many squeezes, and in what order.
reset_notes: Hold the release button until the bag is flat and slide it out. Lift the left corner by hand, take the loose packer out and set the corner down on the sill. Put the packer, the bag, the hose (straight) and the bulb (button up) back on their marks, and check that the right packer has not moved. Nothing is consumed. Safety in real trials: the arms never carry the window; the wedge lifts one corner by at most 16 mm (the head stops it) and a failure drops it that far onto the sill. The head plates keep the window in the opening, with a cord from its top rail to the head as a second restraint. Use a window glazed with toughened or laminated glass. Nobody puts a hand under the frame while the bag is inflated.
fidelity: Real sizes and masses. The frame is rigid and can only rock in its own plane on its packed right corner, which is fixed; a real one can also slide. The bag is two rigid sheets driven apart 1.2 mm per full squeeze of the bulb (its side pushed in 12 mm, 20 N), up to 12 mm, sinking 8 mm/s while the button (3 mm, 3 N) is held; a real bag bulges and lifts less as the load grows. The hose is two stiff links on three joints. Glass can't break.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it never touched the air wedge: the bulb was not squeezed and the corner stayed on the sill; it nudged the loose packer about 1 cm); demo: 1.0
